tagline: Country where the fence posts were cut from limestone.
intro: Out of Lucas, K-232 runs south through the Smoky Hills, crosses the top of Wilson Dam and follows the east shore of Wilson Lake down to Interstate 70. For nearly half the way the lake is alongside. Wilson, proclaimed the Czech Capital of Kansas by a governor in 1967, is two miles on, with the World's Largest Czech Egg.

The fences explain the name. Settlers found grass here and next to no timber, so they split posts out of one thin bed of limestone, drilling holes halfway through and hammering in wedges, each post weighing 250 to 450 pounds. No other place is said to have fenced itself so thoroughly with a single rock.

moments.title: Garden of Eden, Lucas
moments.text: A Union veteran who took up sculpture in retirement filled his lot with concrete figures of his politics and faith, and the tour includes him, in a glass-lidded concrete coffin.

moments.title: Carved fence posts
moments.text: Near Lucas a California sculptor carved the faces of four Lucas residents into four stone posts standing in the fences along the byway.

moments.title: Wilson Dam
moments.text: The road runs along the top of the dam, over a mile of earth fill holding a lake planned partly for irrigation until the salty Saline River ruled that out.
